title: Flipping an Image
statement: `image` is an `n x n` grid of 0s and 1s. First mirror it left to right, so that every row is read in reverse order; then complement it, turning each 0 into 1 and each 1 into 0. Return the grid that results.
notes:
## Intuition

The direct way builds a reversed copy of each row and then flips every bit. Both steps can happen in one pass, in place: the value that lands at position `left` is the complement of the value that was at `right`, and the other way round. Two pointers walking inward from the ends of a row handle each pair once.

## Approach

1. For each `row`, start `left` at 0 and `right` at the last index.
2. While `left < right`, save the complement of `row[left]` in `temp`, write the complement of `row[right]` into `row[left]`, and write `temp` into `row[right]`. Then move both pointers inward.
3. When the row has odd length the pointers meet on the middle cell, which stays in place but must still be complemented.
4. Return the changed `image`.

## Example 1, step by step

Row `[1, 1, 0]`: `left = 0`, `right = 2`; `temp = 1 ^ 1 = 0`, `row[0] = 0 ^ 1 = 1`, `row[2] = 0`, giving `[1, 1, 0]`. Now both pointers are at 1, so the middle flips to 0: `[1, 0, 0]`.
Row `[1, 0, 1]` becomes `[0, 0, 0]` after the outer swap and `[0, 1, 0]` after the middle flip. Row `[0, 0, 0]` becomes `[1, 1, 1]`. The result is `[[1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [1, 1, 1]]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): every cell is read and written once.
- Space: O(1) extra: the grid is changed in place.

## Pitfalls

- Forgetting the middle cell of an odd-length row leaves it uncomplemented.
- Complementing both ends but not swapping them (or swapping without complementing) only does half the job.
- `value ^ 1` (or `1 - value`) complements a bit; `~value` gives -1 or -2, not 0 or 1.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `row` | the row being processed, changed in place |
| `left`, `right` | pointers moving inward from the two ends of the row |
| `temp` | the complemented value from `left`, saved before it is overwritten |

narration.2: Each row is mirrored and complemented on its own.
narration.3: One pointer starts at the row's first cell...
narration.4: ...and the other at its last cell.
narration.5: Keep going while the pointers still mark two different cells.
narration.6: Save the complement of the left value before it is overwritten.
narration.7: The left cell receives the complement of the right value.
narration.8: The right cell receives the saved complement of the left value.
narration.12: In an odd-length row the pointers meet on the middle cell...
